title: Stable but Wrong: When Learning Stabilizes Away from the Truth
abstract: arXiv:2603.21491v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Stable training is often treated as evidence that learning is succeeding, but stability characterizes optimization behavior rather than correctness relative to an external objective. We study what happens when the signal being optimized remains persistently biased. We define Stable but Wrong (SBW) as a learning state in which the learning process remains stable under a task-appropriate operational criterion while the learned outcome remains systematically displaced from an independently defined objective. A minimal strongly convex model shows that a persistent bias in the update direction can shift the unique convergence point away from the true optimum. Controlled experiments in reinforcement learning, supervised learning, and continual fine-tuning of a large language model reveal a recurring separation between apparently normal optimization and correctness under static and feedback-coupled biases. translated_title: 稳定但错误：当学习稳定化偏离真相时
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.21491v2 公告类型：替换 摘要：稳定训练常被视为学习成功的证据，但稳定性描述的是优化行为，而非相对于外部目标的正确性。我们研究了当被优化的信号持续存在偏差时会发生什么。我们将“稳定但错误”（SBW）定义为一种学习状态，在该状态下，学习过程在任务适当的操作标准下保持稳定，而学习结果却系统地偏离独立定义的目标。一个最小强凸模型表明，更新方向上的持续偏差可以将唯一收敛点移离真实最优值。在强化学习、监督学习以及大型语言模型的持续微调中的受控实验揭示了，在静态和反馈耦合偏差下，表面正常的优化与正确性之间反复出现的分离。恢复阶段干净数据的访问……
tldr: 本文提出“稳定但错误”（SBW）概念，证明即使在优化过程稳定收敛的情况下，持续偏差也可能使学习结果系统性偏离真实目标，并在多种学习场景中验证了这一现象。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the concept of "Stable but Wrong" (SBW), demonstrating that even with stable optimization convergence, persistent biases can systematically shift learning outcomes away from the true objective, validated across multiple learning scenarios.
